mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment rises but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Combined weakness in unemployment and payroll employment suggests economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies indicate weakness but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing consumer price index suggests inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI increases but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth above 1% indicates strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies decline but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing payroll growth in late-cycle expansion signals economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If payroll growth slows but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.
